attempts.reason: The first reset recipe did not clear insert mode from the dirty alternate setup. The pinned text/cursor check passed, but the stricter effect failed. Parent publication refused the disagreement before issuing a receipt; raw attempt retained unchanged.

Valid original receipt and pinned results retained. Codex later found that alternate-only DECOM setup could restore a clean main bank and mask an incomplete API reset. Not used for current positive conclusions.
Removed dynamic parent callback execution and independently replayed pinned results; complete receipt retained. Superseded by the same later Codex dirty-main DECOM finding.
Unexpected input at the initial ASCII fence. Stopped before the gap experiments; no semantic verdict or positive claim is taken from this attempt.

Final API explicitly normalizes the promised modes. Three measured API calls include a standalone dirty main screen and dirty main before alternate entry. Full chain remeasured after independent-replay and Codex control fixes; receipt and cleanup completed.

rows.name: Reset bold/dim (SGR 22)
rows.siteRequirement: Send \x1b[1m X \x1b[22m Y, verify the second cell has bold=false and dim=false .
rows.catalogueRequirement: In a headless backend, compare neutral C, bold/dim/italic X, and SGR 22 Y: bold and dim must clear while italic remains. Missing style readback makes the attempted reset check PROBE INVALID; a TTY cursor reply does not verify styling. App: before any attribute is set, draw YY and save with DECSC. For each of the seven nonempty subsets of bold, faint and italic, draw YY with the subset set, then restore with DECRC: every subset must change the crop and every restore must return it exactly. The italic-only crop must differ from the original and every other subset crop. Then set all three, draw YY, send the made-up SGR 99 and draw YY: the crop must not change. Send SGR 22 and draw YY. Supported: the crop equals the italic-only crop. Unsupported: the crop equals the original or a different subset crop. A change at the made-up SGR, or a crop matching neither, is PROBE INVALID. On a multiplexer a negative stays PROBE TODO naming the outer terminal. If a subset, restore or expected-crop separation does not qualify, DECRQSS decides, and a silent DECRQSS keeps the row named refusal.
rows.frozenRequirement: In a headless backend, compare neutral C, bold/dim/italic X, and SGR 22 Y: bold and dim must clear while italic remains. Missing style readback makes the attempted reset check TEST FAILURE; a TTY cursor reply does not verify styling.
rows.pinnedCriterion: measured setup attributes clear on Y and unrelated attributes remain set
rows.rationale: The current upstream catalogue adds a seven-subset App raster test with DECSC/DECRC and an SGR 99 negative control. Fresh stored bold/dim/italic flags satisfy the pinned parser criterion and the live page, but that newer App raster contract was not measured.

rows.catalogueRequirement: In a headless backend, compare neutral C, bold/italic/underlined X, and SGR 0 Y: all three measured attributes must clear. Missing setup readback makes the attempted reset check PROBE INVALID; a TTY cursor reply does not verify styling. App: before any attribute is set, draw YY and save with DECSC. For each of the seven subsets of bold, italic and inverse, draw YY with the subset set, then restore with DECRC: every subset must change the crop and every restore must return it exactly. Then set all three, draw YY, send the made-up SGR 99 and draw YY: the crop must not change. Send SGR 0 and draw YY. Supported: the crop equals the original. Unsupported: the crop equals a subset's crop. A change at the made-up SGR, or a crop matching neither, is PROBE INVALID. On a multiplexer a crop equal to a subset stays PROBE TODO naming the outer terminal. If a subset or restore does not qualify, DECRQSS decides, and a silent DECRQSS keeps the row's named refusal.
rows.frozenRequirement: In a headless backend, compare neutral C, bold/italic/underlined X, and SGR 0 Y: all three measured attributes must clear. Missing setup readback makes the attempted reset check TEST FAILURE; a TTY cursor reply does not verify styling.

rows.name: Hide cursor (DECTCEM)
rows.siteRequirement: Send ESC [ ? 25 l (DECTCEM reset) and verify the cursor is no longer visible.
rows.catalogueRequirement: Headless: measure initial visibility, establish a shown control, check the hidden state and verify restoration. App: with a measured raster, compare the cursor cell raw-pixel digest across shown, hidden and restored frames. Support needs the hidden digest to differ and the restored digest to equal the control; if the attempted check cannot establish a visible control or restored frame, it is PROBE INVALID. DECRQM mode 25 reports the state when no raster is available. If neither a measured raster nor usable DECRQM replies are available, the result is PROBE TODO: shown, hidden and restored frames are captured as evidence, and capture alone does not establish support.
rows.frozenRequirement: Headless: measure initial visibility, establish a shown control, check the hidden state and verify restoration. App: with a measured raster, compare the cursor cell raw-pixel digest across shown, hidden and restored frames. Support needs the hidden digest to differ and the restored digest to equal the control; if the attempted check cannot establish a visible control or restored frame, it is TEST FAILURE. DECRQM mode 25 reports the state when no raster is available. If neither a measured raster nor usable DECRQM replies are available, the result is TEST TODO: shown, hidden and restored frames are captured as evidence, and capture alone does not establish support.
rows.pinnedCriterion: stored cursor visibility changes shown to hidden and the initial state is restored
rows.rationale: The independently rederived contract directly observes stored cursor visibility changes shown to hidden and the initial state is restored.

App: before any attribute is set, draw YY and save with DECSC. For each of the seven subsets of bold, italic and inverse, draw YY with the subset set, then restore with DECRC: every subset must change the crop and every restore must return it exactly. Then set all three, draw YY, send the made-up SGR 99 and draw YY: the crop must not change. Send SGR 0 and draw YY. Supported: the crop equals the original. Unsupported: the crop equals a subset's crop. A change at the made-up SGR, or a crop matching neither, is PROBE INVALID. On a multiplexer a crop equal to a subset stays PROBE TODO naming the outer terminal. If a subset or restore does not qualify, DECRQSS decides, and a silent DECRQSS keeps the row's named refusal.
